sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:167104
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 15838 of 2021

Applicant :- Madan Lal
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Vineet Kumar Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.

1. Heard Shri Abhishek Dwivedi, holding brief of Shri Vineet Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the
applicant, learned Aga and perused the material available on record.
2.

This application for anticipatory bail has been filed by applicant- Madan Lal in connection with Case Crime No. 0234 of 2020, under sections 347, 365, 419, 420, 423, 467, 468, 504, 506 IPC, P.S.
Brijmanganj, District Maharajganj.
3.

It is alleged in the F.I.R. that the present applicant obtained a sale deed in favour of co-accused,
Sangeeta Chaudhary or the father of the informant, who was an insane person without paying any consideration amount.
F.I.R. was lodged on 12.10.2020, which is culminated into charge sheet.

3. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
Charge sheet in the matter has been submitted.

In case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and Madan Lal vs State Of U.P And Another on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199153533/
1 would obey all conditions of bail.

entities.text: Madan Lal vs State Of U.P And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. It is further submitted that the sale deed has been executed after paying a requisite consideration amount and the vendor has executed the sale deed with his own free will and consent and without any coercion.
It is next submitted that the dispute is purely of civil nature and an effort has been made to give it a colour of criminal case.

It is further submitted that applicant has no criminal history to his credit and he is not a vendor or vendee or even witness in the alleged sale deed and no consideration amount or wrongful gain has been received by the present applicant.

It is further submitted that during the course of investigation, the applicant has been cooperative with the I.O. of the case and now after filing of the charge sheet, he is entitled for anticipatory bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
5. In the present matter, the interim protection was granted to the present applicant by this Court vide order dated 20.09.2021 and the same has not been misused by the applicant so far.
It also appears from the record that charge sheet has been submitted in this matter and now no custodial interrogation is required.

6. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled the controversy finally by holding the anticipatory bail need not be of limited duration invariably.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appropriate case, it can continue upto conclusion of trial.
It has been further held therein that anticipatory bail granted can, depending on the conduct and behavior of the accused, continue after filing of the charge sheet till end of trial.

It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

7. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, in my view, it is a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant till conclusion of trial in the matter.
8.
The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

9. In the event of arrest of the applicant in the aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :-
Madan Lal vs State Of U.P And Another on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199153533/
2

entities.text: Madan Lal vs State Of U.P And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(iv) The applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court and if they have passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.

10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the Investigating Officer shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail of the applicant in accordance with law.
